speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on the six-month pilot programme by SMRT Taxis to progressively equip its fleet of 2,800 taxis with booster seats for young children; and (b) whether the pilot will be extended to all taxis companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just concerned why we are looking at utilisation rate versus safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I urge MOH to look into this as more of a safety issue rather than how many people are going to use it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, I hope we do not look at it as practicality versus safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The practicality concerns are addressed already because nowadays, as I have showed the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, the child car seats are really compact; so, it does not take up much space.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, some of the booster seats can fit under the driver's seat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, there is no issue of practicality and again, I hope we look at this at the safety angle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But somehow, I find it strange that the same car, same model, when it becomes a taxi, the safety considerations just disappear.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Senior Parliamentary Secretary can clarify why.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As always, every policy needs to strike a good balance, and in this case, for taxi drivers, the cost and also, operational considerations for them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Taxi drivers make multiple trips throughout the day, serving the diverse needs of different passengers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, we came to this position after public consultation with different stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Naturally, there was a range of views and one, as advocated by the Member Louis Ng, was that there should not be any compromise.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, all children in all vehicles must be in a booster seat or seat harness.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But taxi operators did highlight the constraints because taxis need to satisfy a boot size requirement for luggage or things carried by passengers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If we add on the booster seat requirement, it may pose a challenge, especially for the new hybrid car models which tend to have a smaller boot.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Also, this current exemption will facilitate taxis to offer street hail service for commuters with young children.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Because the "flag, board and go" nature of street hails will be slowed down when the taxi drivers need to fix up the booster seats when stopping alongside the road.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This also may lead to some unhappiness among families with multiple young children, because they will need multiple taxis as there may not be sufficient child restraints in a single vehicle; or a larger capacity taxi with the various seats.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, it means that higher costs will be incurred on the families.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Because PHCs are pre-booked, the passengers can indicate upfront, the seats required and the drivers have ample notice to prepare the seats for the passengers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Today, most if not, all parents of young children should be quite savvy in using ride-hailing apps.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Therefore, I seek the Member's and parents' understanding that the current position does offer options and it strikes a good balance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I agree with Senior Parliamentary Secretary that there is a cost concern, but I hope then it is not the third element where it is cost versus safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am speaking up for the private hire drivers as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We make it compulsory for them, for PHCs that they have to be in car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Then again, it is a bit strange that for taxis, it is not.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The rationale given is because taxis do street hails.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But really, how many street hails are there nowadays, for the taxis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think a lot of them are based on bookings as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: For parents with young children, I really doubt that in today's context, they would actually do street hail.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: They would also book the taxis rather than go down on the streets and try and flag one down.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Safety for all people, especially young children, is important.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I think while safety is important, but we really also need to consider other implications, especially when it affects the livelihood of people.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One option we could look at, I think, if we see that there is a need for it, would be good to look at maybe ride-hail type of journeys to look into.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But we will continue to consult and work with the different stakeholders as we look into this area.
